newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish LOT to order 8 Boeing 737s.
newsitem.headline: Polish LOT to order 8 Boeing 737s.

text.p: Polish national airline PLL LOT plans to order eight Boeing 737-800 planes late this year or early in 1997, LOT's deputy president told a news conference on Wednesday.
"A contract for the purchase of eight new Boeings (737) should be signed at the turn of the year," Bazyli Samojlik said.
Samojlik was speaking after the official signing of an earlier announced delivery contract of two Boeing 737-800 aircraft.

LOT's president Jan Litwinski, also present, said the Polish airline had already discussed on Wednesday a delivery option of the eight Boeing 737-800 aircraft with representatives of Boeing Commercial Airplane Group.
"Today LOT talked about the option for the delivery of the eight airplanes from 1999 to 2002," Litwinski said.
Samojlik said the contract would boost LOT's fleet of mid-range airplanes to 23.
He said the planned order for the eight 737-800 planes would be worth about $360 million.
Under the $90 million contract signed on Wednesday Boeing would deliver two of its 737-800 planes in May 1998, he said.

Samojlik also said the delivery of two 737-400 planes ordered last July, worth $70 million, was scheduled for May 1997. Also in May 1997 LOT expected the delivery of a long-distance B767 aircraft purchased last July.
He said LOT was likely to stop ordering the B767 aircraft and Litwinski signalled the airline was considering a purchase of Boeing's new 777 long-range plane before the year 2000.
"We are considering buying a 777 as a significant option," Litwinski said.
LOT currently has 11 Boeing 737 mid-range planes, four long-range Boeing 767s and eight ATR 72 short-distance turboprop machines.
